task.title: Pair coordinates with zip and unpacking
task.statement:
This turns two equal-length parallel lists of coordinates into "x,y" label strings. It walks both lists by index and pokes at the pair with [0]/[1] instead of unpacking it.

    def label_points(xs, ys):
        labels = []
        for i in range(len(xs)):
            pair = (xs[i], ys[i])
            labels.append(str(pair[0]) + "," + str(pair[1]))
        return labels

Rewrite it idiomatically in solution.py; same name, same behavior — assume xs and ys are always the same length. (Hint: zip the two lists, unpack each pair into named variables, and format with an f-string.)
task.notes:
Micro-drill. If they ask whether an approach 'counts', say idiomatic means what a fluent reviewer would write today; no other resolutions to give. Targets: pair-not-unpacked, index-loop, append-transform-loop.

Idiomatic reference (for your judgment and post-pass debriefs; never hand it over before their run passes):
def label_points(xs, ys):
    return [f"{x},{y}" for x, y in zip(xs, ys)]
task.appendix:
Targets: pair-not-unpacked, index-loop, append-transform-loop

Hidden checks (behavior must be preserved):
assert label_points([1, 2], [3, 4]) == ["1,3", "2,4"]
assert label_points([], []) == []
assert label_points([0], [-5]) == ["0,-5"]
assert label_points([1.5], [2]) == ["1.5,2"]
assert label_points([10, 20, 30], [1, 2, 3]) == ["10,1", "20,2", "30,3"]

Idiomatic reference:
def label_points(xs, ys):
    return [f"{x},{y}" for x, y in zip(xs, ys)]
